#1293. Thomas Frank Already Has His Own Bryan Mbeumo at Crystal Palace in Yeremy Pino

Crystal Palace have parted ways with Pierre Sage and are expected to reach an agreement with Thomas Frank as the Frenchman's successor.

The Eagles have endured a dismal start to the new campaign, winning just two of their first ten matches — a return that has them rock bottom of the Premier League table. Sage has subsequently lost his job, with Steve Parish set to turn to former Brentford boss Frank to save his team from relegation.

The Dane has been out of a job since being sacked by Tottenham Hotspur in February. Appointed as Ange Postecoglou's replacement in N17 at the beginning of last term, Frank's league win rate of 26.9% was the worst of any Tottenham manager in the Premier League era before his successor, Igor Tudor, eclipsed him.

This stint in North London has certainly damaged the 53-year-old's reputation, but it could ultimately make him an ideal option for Palace. In the short term, the South Londoners need a coach who can fix their leaky defence and simply steady the ship. In the long term, they need someone who can platform their more talented offensive players by building on this solid foundation. Frank is capable of doing both, while he's unlikely to be poached by a bigger club in the process, after already failing to impress at Tottenham.

In order to succeed at Selhurst Park, he'll need some talented individuals who can replicate the transition-heavy football his Brentford side mastered.

In Adam Wharton, he has the passing midfielder who can single-handedly carry the progression load that was carried by the likes of Christian Norgaard and Mathias Jensen. In Jean-Philippe Mateta, he has his Ivan Toney — the surprisingly technically gifted target man who provides the team with a focal point, and crucially, goals.

There are, however, question marks over who might replicate the roles of some of the supporting cast. Bryan Mbeumo became a significant figure in Frank's Brentford team, and some may argue that there's no obvious analogous player at Palace. They'd be wrong.

During Toney's spell at Brentford under Frank, Mbeumo dovetailed excellently with the target man striker, doing the running for him off the ball. The England international would impose himself physically on the opponent's centre-backs, specifically in the air, before playing in Mbeumo, who'd constantly be making diagonal runs beyond the centre-forward.

In closer quarters, the two players would combine neatly, playing quick one-twos around the opposition before carving open opportunities. It's not difficult to envisage Mateta and Yeremy Pino reproducing some of these passing patterns, implemented by Frank and his coaching staff.

Pino, who has endured a few turbulent performances of late, is generally an excellent technician who shares some similarities with Mbeumo. While the Spaniard is not quite as direct a goal threat as his Cameroonian counterpart — in terms of making runs in behind — both players are naturally stocky and use this frame to their advantage when it comes to dribbling.

Statistical Comparison 2025/26 (League Only)

They're both eager to get shots off on the right-hand side of the box as often as possible, and look to manipulate the ball to create separation from defenders using similar techniques.

Mbeumo scored 20 goals and provided eight assists in his final season at Brentford under Frank, reflecting his importance to the Danish coach. Pino managed just five goals and five assists last season for Palace, but it's not difficult to envisage Frank eliciting more from him by using him similarly to the now Manchester United star.

Ismaila Sarr is always likely to be the primary goalscoring wide forward at Palace, with the Senegalese forward is more analogous to someone like Kevin Schade. His primary attribute is to arrive on the end of moves, rather than getting involved in build-up play.

Pino, like Mbeumo, is capable of doing both sides of the game, with an emphasis on creativity and playmaking in and around the box.

Crystal Palace are considering sacking Pierre Sage, and two players should follow him out the door if he does go.

#1290. Youngsters will get their chance, Bruno Fernandes can thrive and touchline energy will be vital: Key lessons for Man United from incoming boss Mauricio Pochettino's 6-0 USA masterclass

Published: 18:47 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 05:54 EST, 16 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino enjoyed a stellar penultimate game in charge of the United States, thrashing Haiti 6-0.

The newly appointed Manchester United manager has just one game left before sinking his teeth into the job at Old Trafford.

He will link up with United on Wednesday, but first must navigate the second leg of their Concacaf Nations League quarter-final tie with Haiti on Tuesday.

Here, Pochettino cut a fairly reserved figure on the touchline as he was rewarded for trusting youth - and even saw his team score from a corner, something United don't do much of these days.

Without further ado, here are four things Manchester United fans learned from the win.

Mauricio Pochettino, dressed in a scarf, was fairly reserved as the United States beat Haiti 6-0

Pochettino’s arrival spells good news for United’s proud tradition of promoting homegrown youth - it is glad tidings for the likes of Shea Lacey and Kobbie Mainoo. You wonder if, for a while, JJ Gabriel will look on forlornly from Real Madrid’s reserves.

The Argentinian handed out 13 debuts in the September-October international break, including to eight teenagers in one 4-1 victory over Peru.

His strategy was no different here as he started 18-year-old Julian Hall up front and Diego Kochen, 20, in goal - both players he has given debuts to this year. He was rewarded, with Hall scoring his fourth goal in just five games for the United States, while Kochen kept a clean sheet.

Despite his affinity for the stars of tomorrow, he is a hard schoolmaster. In a column for The Athletic in 2022, he revealed that he sat a young Harry Kane down for a brutal meeting where he showed him stats and clips to justify why he wasn’t playing him more.

Pochettino had known Kane’s potential from their first training session but wanted the ‘tough conversation’ to get the best out of him. Kane went on to score 169 goals under him for Tottenham, and now he’s the best player in the world.

His trust in fresh faces could inject some much-needed enthusiasm around the club, strengthen the squad's connection with the fanbase, and increase the energy levels in one of the Premier League's oldest, most lethargic teams.

The likes of Shea Lacey will be delighted at how Pochettino puts trust in younger players

Julian Hall, 18, struck his fourth goal in five games for the United States under Pochettino

Pochettino has a history of getting the most out of attacking midfielders such as Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen, and Adam Lallana. You can add Cole Palmer to that list too, though he was primarily a right winger under him at Chelsea.

Manchester United desperately need him to get a tune out of Bruno Fernandes, who has cut a frustrated figure this season and whose creative efficiency has declined - though he still has nine goal involvements.

If Christian Pulisic’s performance against Haiti is anything to go by, Fernandes will be happy. The attacking midfielder scored twice, playing a free role and being given penalty duty.

The 28-year-old was also asked to muck in defensively, and that’s something Fernandes is willing to do. Across the seasons, he has often covered more ground than any of his team-mates.

Pochettino and Pulisic have seemingly had a distant relationship, despite the latter’s insistence to the contrary. The manager branded it ‘b*******’ when the AC Milan star opted out of the Gold Cup last year, and left him out of his selection a couple of months ago, bringing in 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan.

Asked about Pochettino's upcoming final game, Pulisic said at full-time: 'We're treating it like any other game.' No emotion on display.

Depending on how you interpret Fernandes - either a die-for-the-badge club servant or a primadonna - Pochettino could draw the best or worst out of the Portuguese.

Pochettino often gets the best out of attacking midfielders - will he work well with Bruno Fernandes?

He has had a distant relationship with Christian Pulisic, but the AC Milan star scored twice here

Pochettino tends to push his defensive lines high up the pitch and his strategy with the United States has been no different.

They were almost caught out for trying to play the offside trap early on as a simple ball from midfield sent Danley Jean Jacques through one-on-one, forcing Kochen into a good save.

Meanwhile, full-backs Antonee Robinson and Alex Freeman were constantly pushing high and overlapping in his 4-2-3-1 system - although you’d obviously expect a strong level of intent when they’re favourites against Haiti.

Given his high-line tradition, Pochettino may well favour more mobile defenders such as Leny Yoro and Patrick Dorgu.

The battle for Harry Maguire will be to convince his new boss that his other qualities compensate for his lack of pace.

Pochettino takes inspiration from the frenetic football of Marcelo Bielsa, who managed him at Newell’s Old Boys in Argentina.

But he'll have to balance his philosophy with the reality of United's woeful defensive record this campaign. Just the 15 goals conceded in the last five games...

Pochettino showed an eagerness to intervene early in the game - a possible boost after Michael Carrick suffered from slow starts

Pochettino is typically seen as an animated character on the touchline, in contrast to Carrick's statesmanlike behaviour, but he spent lots of time in his seat here.

He has calmed down somewhat these days - though he did kick a crate of bottles in frustration at the World Cup - and didn’t even react much when his team scored.

A major criticism of Carrick is that he takes too long to change things in-game, often going late with substitutions. Pochettino has traditionally leaned that way, too, but he was eager to influence proceedings here.

Even three minutes in, at a break while Antonee Robinson was being treated, he called Pulisic over for what looked like an intense tactical chat.

United have been plagued by slow starts this season, so it was encouraging to see Pochettino so alert and full of ideas early into the game. He could have coasted, really, but wanted to eke out every advantage.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of this Europa League tie between Bournemouth and AC Milan at the Vitality Stadium.

Back in 2008, Bournemouth’s prospect of a European meeting with Milan seemed impossible. After entering administration with crippling debts of around £4m, Bournemouth were handed a 10-point deduction and relegated from League One. To make matters worse, a hefty 17-point deduction was given to the club ahead of the 2008-09 League Two season, with relegation to non-league seeming inevitable. However, midway through the campaign, the transformative Eddie Howe was parachuted in as Bournemouth’s saviour, eventually guiding the club to safety.

Fast forward to October 2026 in an extraordinary rise and Bournemouth are competing in their first-ever European campaign in the club’s 127-year existence. They welcome Milan to Dorset, having earned back-to-back victories over Real Sociedad and Sturm Graz to kick off their inaugural Europa League adventure in style.

Now, they host the second most successful side in the European Cup history. In terms of heritage and silverware, these clubs could not be further apart, but on the pitch, it’s incredibly tough to call.

On Sunday, Marco Rose’s Bournemouth picked up their first Premier League win of the season, beating 10-man Sunderland 2-0 at the Vitality thanks to goals from Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson to move out of the relegation zone.

Meanwhile, Ruben Amorim is in charge at Milan and returns to England after a tumultuous 14-month reign at Manchester United, where he was sacked in January. Milan lost their opening Europa League fixture 2-0 at home to Benfica, before battering Salzburg 4-0 in Austria, with Alphadjo Cisse netting a stunning hat-trick.

Crystal Palace are also in the Europa League tonight and face an incredibly daunting away trip to Turkish side Besiktas. Pressure is firmly on manager Pierre Sage following the 5-0 humiliation against Brighton last weekend and a shaky start to the season. Palace lost 3-2 to Sage’s former employers Lyon in their previous Europa League outing, with a positive performance and result needed to restore the fans’ faith.

Both games kick-off at 20:00, with team news coming imminently.

#1286. Massive atlas of brain region linked to a host of diseases is the most detailed yet

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Miryam Naddaf is a reporter for Nature in London.

An MRI scan of the basal ganglia, seen here in section and colour-coded.Credit: Zephyr/SPL

The basal ganglia are groups of cells that sit deep in the brain and process motor, cognitive, mood and decision-making information. They are linked to neurodegenerative and psychiatric conditions from Parkinson’s and Huntington’s disease to schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and addiction.

Now, researchers have published the world’s most-detailed atlas of basal ganglia so far, comprising 25.5 million brain cells from humans, macaques and marmosets. The work is described in a collection of 26 papers published in Cell, Cell Reports, Cell Reports Methods, Cell Systems, Cell Genomics and Neuron. The research includes understudied neurons1, provides insights about how some brain cells change with age2 and suggests which might be linked to diseases3.

The atlas, a collaboration between hundreds of scientists in nine countries, is part of the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) — a US$500-million project launched in 2022 by the US National Institutes of Health aimed at creating reference maps of mammalian brains.

“It’s a massive dictionary that we needed in the field,” says Ana Muñoz-Manchado, a neuroscientist at the University of Cádiz in Spain, who studies the basal ganglia in neurodegenerative disorders.

The basal ganglia atlas contains 21 million cells from the brains of six humans, three million cells from three rhesus and cynomolgus macaques, and 1.5 million cells from two marmosets4. The researchers also used data from previously published maps of the whole mouse brain5,6.

By comparing the basal ganglia between the primate species, the researchers identified 61 cell types in humans, macaques and marmosets that have been conserved over 76 million years3.

The team analysed brain tissue samples from different developmental stages across the lifespan of the species. The latest work combines information about these cells in unprecedented detail, from measurements of their gene expression and DNA modifications that control gene regulation to recordings of their electrical activity, as well as how DNA is folded inside their nuclei.

The researchers also mapped where each cell is located in the brain and designed a common framework to characterize and annotate the cells. It is “essentially a scaffold on which we can now fairly readily complete the rest of the brain”, explains Michael Hawrylycz, a bioinformatician at the Allen Institute for Brain Science in Seattle, Washington, who took part in the project.

One study examined 1.1 million cells in the basal ganglia’s largest structure — known as the striatum — from 19 deceased human donors7. Unlike many other brain areas, the striatum has no neat anatomical boundaries. The researchers identified six zones in the human and macaque striatum that had distinct molecular signatures, each containing distinct populations of neurons and glial cells.

“The cells in these zones all look the same under the microscope, but have very strong transcriptional differences and are strikingly consistent from person to person,” said co-author Evan Macosko, a neurobiologist at the Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in a press release from the institute.

Macosko and his colleagues also found that gene expression patterns that distinguished each zone from the other became increasingly similar with age, particularly in brain regions affected by Huntington’s or Parkinson’s disease.

Another study analysed nearly four million cells in the striatum and prefrontal cortex from 178 deceased adult donors aged from 27 to more than 902. The researchers found that the cellular make-up of the two brain regions varied between people, particularly for non-neuronal cells known as glial cells. This underscores the need for brain cell atlases to account for these individual differences.

#1285. Celtic Signed The ‘Next Henrik Larsson’, He Scored 0 Goals and Retired At 29

Eight years after signing for Celtic and being compared to Henrik Larsson, Mohamed Bangura retired from football at the age of 29.

Born in Kambia in Sierra Leone, Bangura joined FC Kallon, one of the top clubs in his home country, at a young age. Impressing for the Freetown-based club, he made the switch to Europe, playing for two different Swedish sides before earning his big move to Celtic in 2011.

He'd go on to make just 16 appearances for the Scottish giants, before joining Istanbul Basksehir in 2014 after having had his contract at Celtic Park terminated by mutual consent.

After leaving Turkey, he spent time in China and back in Sweden, before eventually hanging up his boots in 2019 after failing to find a new club following his release from Superettan side Dalkurd.

An extremely prolific number nine in Sierra Leone's top flight for Kallon, several clubs across Europe were keeping tabs on Bangura's development towards the end of the 2000s. Swedish third division side IFK Varnamo were able to negotiate a short-term loan with Kallon for the young striker, and in March 2010, he made his way to Scandinavia to commence his career in Europe.

After scoring 12 goals in 13 league appearances for Varnamo, Swedish giants AIK swept in and signed Bangura on a three-and-a-half-year deal. The Stockholm club fought off considerable interest from multiple potential suitors, with the player already garnering significant attention in Sweden at this point in his development.

Quick, intelligent and an expert finisher, there was a lot to like about the then 21-year-old. After just over 12 months at AIK, which saw 14 goals in 35 appearances, Celtic forked out £2.1 million to sign the Sierra Leonean. According to BBC Sport, Bangura had been recommended to the Glaswegian outfit by club legend Henrik Larsson, who had been closely observing the striker's progress in Sweden.

"I'm flattered that someone like Henrik Larsson would recommend me," Bangura said at the time.

"I know all about what a great player he was for Celtic. I am delighted to be joining a club the size of Celtic."

Naturally, Larsson's endorsement led many to tip Bangura to emulate the legendary forward's achievements at Celtic Park. The Swede scored 242 goals in 313 appearances for Celtic between 1997 and 2004, and the club's supporters were yearning for a similarly productive number nine to replicate these feats.

The pressure this created clearly got to Bangura, who didn't come remotely close to being Larsson's long-term successor. After failing to find the back of the net early on, manager Neil Lennon started favouring strikers Gary Hooper, Anthony Stokes and Georgios Samaras. This fall in the pecking order, combined with a serious knee injury, saw the young centre-forward finish his debut season in Scotland with no goals in just 15 appearances.

The following season, after finding himself on the periphery of Lennon's squad, he returned to AIK on loan. This was the first of two loan spells back in the Scandinavian nation, as he'd later join Elfsborg for a short period, before Celtic opted to terminate his contract in 2014, leaving him searching for a new employer.

In an attempt to resurrect his career, Bangura switched up his surroundings by moving south to Turkey in 2014. Signing for then second-tier side Istanbul Basaksehir, he struggled to break into the team, making just eight appearances before calling it quits in the historic pan-continental city.

AIK granted him another lifeline shortly after, allowing their former striker to train with them as he looked for a new team. After impressing during training, the Swedish outfit signed Bangura for a third time in December 2014. He enjoyed a brief renaissance during the 2015 Allsvenskan season, netting eight goals in 34 appearances.

Instead of remaining in Sweden, he once again opted for a new venture at the end of 2015, joining Chinese Super League side Dalian Yifang on a three-year deal. He only saw out a single year of this contract, with Dalian terminating his deal at the end of the first season after he'd failed to make an impact.

Once again, he was a free agent, and this time it took a lot longer to find a new place to ply his trade. Over a year after being forced out of Dalian, Bangura returned to Sweden again, but this time in the second tier. He signed for Dalkurd, but wasn't offered a new deal at the end of his solitary season with the Superettan side.

Celtic's extensive history has seen many players who are tough, hard, and fierce athletes.

Bangura once again spent over 12 months searching for a new home, but an offer never came. In January 2019, he gave up, calling time on his short-lived career, just eight years after being tipped for greatness at Celtic.

#1284. Ronaldinho day earns Ravenna €199,000 in ticket sales

Ravenna have announced their sold-out Serie C match featuring Ronaldinho’s return to the field earned them €199,000 in ticket sales alone at the Stadio Benelli.

The match against Forlì in the third division of Italian football turned into a global event that was transmitted live in many different countries, an entirely unusual occurrence for a club in the lower leagues.

The Stadio Benelli was even expanded for the event, with a new temporary stand set up and named Tribuna R10 in honour of the Brazilian legend.

The Ravenna press office informed Football Italia that they raked in €199,000 in ticket sales on Sunday, thanks to a 6,743 sold-out crowd at the Stadio Benelli.

Ticket prices were inevitably raised for the big occasion, rising to a maximum of €150 for the hospitality section, but starting at €15 for season ticket holders, and under-14s able to attend for just €10.

Ronaldinho started the match and played the entire first half, using the break to salute the crowd and perhaps bow out for good at the age of 46.

#1283. 'Am I supposed to answer that?': Erling Haaland breaks silence and distances himself from Man City cheating verdict as star striker insists 'I don't really know much... I was playing for Bryne Under 9s'

Published: 09:50 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 06:26 EST, 16 November 2026

Erling Haaland delivered a monologue of over two minutes detailing the teams he represented in the years covered by the Premier League's investigation into Man City, as the star questioned how he was meant to respond to the club's guilty verdict.

Man City were found guilty of the vast majority of charges brought against them by the Premier League for financial wrongdoing when the verdict was released in September. The club have since appealed.

An independent commission ruled Man City had disguised payments worth £900million in a nine-year period with ‘sham’ deals.

Man City were found to have artificially inflated sponsorship agreements and pumped money into the club from its Abu Dhabi owners via disguised payments in a bid to swerve Premier League spending rules.

Haaland was quizzed about the club's situation by Norwegian broadcaster TV2, after scoring in the national team's 3-1 victory over Wales on Saturday.

The Man City star's initial answer lasted for two minutes and 14 seconds, as he reeled off the teams he had represented from 2009 to 2018, the years covered by the charges.

Erling Haaland insisted it was difficult for him to answer a question about Man City's guilty verdict, with the club appealing against the decision of an independent commission. Source: TV2Sport

Haaland stressed he remains happy at the club after being asked about his future given the potential ramificiations if Man City fail with their appeal to overturn the verdict.

'In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list. 2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team,' Haaland began.

'Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

'So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle…

'It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure.'

Haaland continued by listing fellow Norwegians who had been at Man City at the time, joking that they may be in a better place to offer insight.

'There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think,' Haaland said.

'Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can't remember.

The forward distanced himself from the case as he listed team he played from 2009-18, the time covered by the charges. Pictured: Haaland in action for Molde in 2018

'But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it.

'I assume the answers will come… I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

'To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City.

'A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there.'

Man City have continued to insist they had 'irrefutable evidence' proving their innocence, but if the club loses its appeal, the Premier League have a range of sanctions at their disposal – including relegation or expulsion.

Haaland, who has won eight major honours at the club including the Treble in 2023, was asked about whether the case has affected his thoughts on his Man City future.

'I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,' Haaland responded.

'I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

'I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we're top of our group in Europe.

'Things aren't going so well for City in the league, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can't focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.'

Man City have won twice and lost three times in the Premier League since the independent commission verdict was announced in September.

Enzo Maresca's side have slipped to six points behind reigning champions Arsenal following their drop off in form.

#1282. Man Utd Ready to Sign Nathan Collins for Mauricio Pochettino

There may be more than six weeks until the January transfer window opens, but Manchester United are already considering how they can back new manager Mauricio Pochettino in the market.

Pochettino was confirmed as Michael Carrick's successor at Man United on Friday, and he will officially leave his role as the United States manager after they play Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning, UK time.

The 54-year-old will then travel to Manchester, where he will only have a couple of days to prepare for his bow against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

It's a difficult fixture for a club who have only won one of their 10 Premier League matches this term, which has left them in the relegation zone as we approach December.

A big improvement is needed on the pitch and Pochettino must find that tune out of the players he has at his disposal, before the club can potentially make additions in January.

Fabrizio Romano has already confirmed that there will be at least one new signing in the New Year, and potentially two or three, with centre-back and striker the two priority positions.

According to talkSPORT reporter Alex Crook, the Red Devils are interested in Fulham duo Calvin Bassey and Antonee Robinson, while Folarin Balogun is a potential target having narrowly missed out on joining Premier League rivals Everton on deadline day in the summer.

Robinson and Balogun have both worked under Pochettino for the USMNT, while Bassey could kill two birds with one stone for the Red Devils given he can play both left-sided centre-back and left-back, amid the possibility that both Lisandro Martinez and Luke Shaw could leave Old Trafford in 2027.

One other player that is being looked at, according to Crook, is Brentford captain Nathan Collins.

Pochettino's Tottenham team was built around a strong leadership team put in place for the Argentine, and it allowed them to thrive.

Goalkeeper Hugo Lloris was club captain for much of the 54-year-old manager's time at Spurs, but he was backed up by Harry Kane and Jan Vertonghen at the time.

Pochettino is inheriting some good leaders on paper at Old Trafford, including captain Bruno Fernandes and Harry Maguire, while the likes of Luke Shaw, Diogo Dalot, Youri Tielemans and Lisandro Martinez offer plenty of experience.

Nathan Collins is unlikely to walk into the Theatre of Dreams and become captain, but the fact that he is currently the skipper of both Brentford and the Republic of Ireland shows what an important addition to the dressing room he would be.

And that is just one of Collins' strengths, given he has established himself as one of the best in his position in the Premier League in recent seasons.

The Irishman, described as 'very talented' by Thomas Frank when he joined the Bees, stands at 6ft 5in tall and is known for his aerial prowess when it comes to winning headed duels, while he has strong tackling and clearance statistics for the Bees.

Brentford are also known to play out from the back, and that is something that Collins has proven he is more than capable of doing, which will suit Pochettino down to the ground.

That quality to make progressive passes from defence is increasingly important in the modern game, and the 25-year-old is capable of that and much more, even if he hasn't been able to show it too much this season because of injury.

Collins for Brentford (Premier League 2026-27)

One thing that could count against Collins is whether the Red Devils actually need a right-sided centre-back, given they already have Maguire, Leny Yoro and Matthijs de Ligt who prefer to play on the right.

There is a greater need for a left-sided player, given there are doubts over Martinez's future and Ayden Heaven is still yet to convince people that he should be a consistent starter.

In those terms, Jarrad Branthwaite of Everton might be a better addition, but Collins could cost a fraction of the price, especially given United and Brentford already have a working relationship after the Bryan Mbeumo deal in 2025.

#1281. Carrick weighs up stripping Bruno Fernandes of Man Utd captaincy

A defiant Michael Carrick refused to rule out stripping Bruno Fernandes of the captaincy as the Manchester United manager told his players to cut out their public sniping and start doing their talking on the pitch.

Carrick struck a bullish tone as he came out fighting and moved to reassert his authority after a tumultuous past fortnight that has left him battling to save his job ahead of Sunday’s must-win game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

The United manager began his press conference on Friday afternoon with a stirring five-and-a-half-minute monologue in which he issued an emotional call to arms to his players to demonstrate the values of hard work, sacrifice, humility and resilience that define the club.

Referencing Sir Matt Busby, Sir Alex Ferguson, Sir Bobby Charlton, Ryan Giggs and Wayne Rooney, Carrick warned there could be no “entitlement” culture in echoes of complaints from his predecessor Ruben Amorim.

United are actively considering their options in the event Carrick cannot quickly arrest a shocking start to the season that hit a new low with Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation by Como. The likes of Julian Nagelsmann, Eddie Howe, Unai Emery, Fabian Hürzeler and Antonio Conte are in the frame.

But Carrick insisted he was “100 per cent” convinced he was the right man to take United forward and, while he claimed the dressing room was “not divided”, he has had to contend with first defender Lisandro Martínez and then Fernandes venting in public.

Martínez was fined and publicly apologised for an extraordinary tirade at Jason Wilcox, the director of football, and the Old Trafford board last week before Fernandes appeared to call out Carrick’s tactics in the wake of the Como debacle.

Carrick responded at the time to having his set-up and approach questioned by suggesting tactics count for little if players are unprepared to run.

Asked if he would consider taking the captaincy off Fernandes, Carrick said: “I’m just saying I’ll always – whatever the situation is – do what’s best for the club.”

Pressed on whether Fernandes’s comments were all the more insidious and divisive at a time when the manager was trying to pull the squad together so soon after Martínez’s outburst, Carrick added: “Yeah, the most important thing for me is the team.

“First and foremost is the squad, the dynamics in the squad. And again, it’s about the club. And I’ll always do what’s best for the club.”

Carrick, Wilcox and United chief executive Omar Berrada held a meeting with Martínez in the wake of his criticism but the manager would not be drawn on whether he had spoken with Fernandes and it remains to be seen if he will be captain or start against Bournemouth.

“If I’ve spoken to him or haven’t spoken to him, I don’t think this is the time to go into too much detail,” he said.

Carrick agreed that United collectively needed to stop turning on each other in public. “We need to move forward in the right direction. We need to do things that enable us to do that. That’s pretty clear,” he said.

“It [the dressing room] is not divided, no. We just need to get back to doing what we do best and we will.”

Separately, Carrick expressed sympathy for Fernandes over the “awful” burglary at his home on Wednesday night when he was in Italy, and said the club “are doing a lot of work to support Bruno and his family”.

Carrick is under huge pressure heading into Bournemouth but said he was happy to take the heat if it enabled his players to perform.

“It is my responsibility whatever goes on the pitch, and what we are as a group, and what we look like, and what we feel like,” he said. “I’ll hold that umbrella for me to get wet and for everyone else to stay dry.”

Nonetheless, Carrick admitted he was “hurting an awful lot” and that the team had to get back to showing the values and qualities that have underpinned the club’s historic success after a “really unacceptable” performance against Como and wider struggles. United have won two of 11 matches this season.

“I’m not entitled to be here,” Carrick said. “We’re not entitled to win. We’ve won in the past, we’ve got an incredible history, but that doesn’t mean you’re entitled to just win.

“I’m fully aware of that. It takes hard work, a lot of sacrifice. You’ve got to invest yourself in the club and you’ve got to do a lot of things that maybe aren’t so nice, but you’ve got to do it for each other, and you’ve got to win.

“It’s important we live up to that, and it’s important for me to push those values, and for our supporters to feel that moving forward.

“We’ve kind of lost our way a bit if I’m honest, and we will get it back. I’m totally confident we’ll get it back. Respect this club, respect what it takes, because it’s very important to me.”

Carrick added that he was inspired by the values of “humility, hard work, resilience, sacrifice and pride” embodied by the likes of Busby, Ferguson, Charlton, Giggs and Rooney.

“We can never lose that, and I won’t let us lose that,” he said. “We’ve had it for a spell, I feel very strongly about that. It inspires me a lot to live up to that and keep driving that with the players.

“There’s a resilience about this club that’s been shown for a long time. Whether that’s bouncing back from adversity, comebacks, late goals, success, sustaining success, there’s a resilience in this club that runs very deep.”

Carrick was trailed by a camera crew from Amazon Prime as he entered the media auditorium at Manchester United’s Carrington training base at 1.30pm on Friday.

There have been plenty of dark moments at Old Trafford in the post-Sir Alex Ferguson era. But the difference this season is that any internal drama will soon be available for public consumption after the decision to allow cameras into a once-sacrosanct dressing room.

Whether Carrick will see out the next week, let alone a season being captured by filmmakers from Amazon’s All Or Nothing series, who probably cannot believe their luck at the unfolding crisis, remains to be seen. He certainly needs a big reaction against Bournemouth at Old Trafford at the very least.

But it became clear as he began his press conference with an emotional 5½-minute monologue that he would not go down without a fight.

#1279. Lamine Yamal Named Ballon d’Or Rival as His Toughest One-on-One Opponent Ever

Lamine Yamal terrorises defenders all over the world, no matter the competition. Whether it's on the way to World Cup glory with Spain or a Champions League at Camp Nou for Barcelona.

The 19-year-old is already one of the best players in world football, having come third in the 2026 Ballon d'Or rankings, behind only Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe.

Tracking the leading contenders to win the prestigious Ballon d'Or award in 2027.

Yamal is viewed as the long-term Lionel Messi successor in football, and it's clear to see why. His fearless dribbling and unwavering confidence are reminiscent of the greatest footballer in history.

Yamal won his first major international honour back in 2024, when he played a starring role in Spain's European Championship triumph. During that tournament, the teenager came up against his toughest opponent, who will surprise many.

He named Germany defender David Raum as the hardest left-back he'd come up against at that point. Raum has been at RB Leipzig since 2022, and was labelled a 'solid defender' by the best young player in the world.

Mendes is undoubtedly one of the finest defenders on the planet as an all-action member of PSG, the back-to-back Champions League winners.

#1278. 'Managers now are b****y boring!': NEIL WARNOCK on the lack of characters in football, his friendship with Pep Guardiola, why he is open to managing again post-Christmas - and how he almost became a chiropodist!

Published: 19:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 08:25 EST, 16 November 2026

Spending time in the company of Neil Warnock is always an education, be it witnessing one of his legendary foul-mouthed touchline rants or perched at one of his stage shows at grand venues like London Palladium.

On this occasion, Daily Mail Sport is perched in an east London bar watching on as one of English football's national treasures is posing for some modelling. Yes, you read that right, Mr Warnock is here to launch his own pair of socks with a tipple of Famous Grouse whisky in hand.

The complements on Warnock's 77-year-old feet are soon over, though, and we can get on to talking about a life in football that started six decades ago as a winger for Chesterfield and has traversed 10 clubs as a player, 17 as a manager and more than 2,000 games in the dugout.

So where to start? Maybe his reflections on nearly five decades in management – and how the whole conversation about feet is not too out of place…

'You don't realise how long it has been really, I started off just a team of ragamuffins as I call them,' he says in his iconic Yorkshire accent. 'They used to train on the green where I had digs in Hartlepool and asked me to coach them.

'I remember we scored from a set-piece we worked on, I was running up and down the touchline high-fiving everyone. I got the bug. I knew I could never get to the top as a player, I was quick but I was brainless.

Daily Mail Sport caught up with Neil Warnock to discuss his six decades in football

After representing 10 different clubs as a player, Warnock became one of the most compelling managers in the game

'I could've been a chiropodist if not in football. That could be on a quiz, couldn't it? I had bad feet at Scunthorpe, I used to get massive blisters so the physio there started getting me to do some of the players' feet.

'I enjoyed doing ingrown toenails and things like that! So I thought why not? Then I had a practice in Sheffield. I had to make a decision when we won the league at Scarborough whether to go full-time or pack it in. I thought, "Oh, go on then, let's give it a little go".

'It's not worked out badly, really, has it?

'People come up to me every day and say, "You're a legend, you". And I say, "Oh, thank you very much". Then they tell me what club they support, I have had so many haven't I? Last week I went out for a minute and had four selfies. They all appreciate what I did for their club.

'There aren't as many characters in the game now, you wouldn't get upset with managers now like in my day because now they are that b****y boring! Some of them barely speak.

'They won't get the rapport we had. I managed at a good time. The way I managed, I needed that humour. I needed the lads to enjoy it. I signed a lot of players that many managers wouldn't touch with a barge pole, are you with me? They ended up getting me promotions.'

The aforementioned humour brings us on to a private conversation he had with the great Pep Guardiola, one of the millions of anecdotes up Warnock's sleeve but one that he has not told until now.

'I went to a training session and he asked me to say a few words,' explains Warnock. 'I said, "Well lads I bet you're glad I'm not your manager because we'd be kicking balls from there to there, chasing it, heading it, practicing our tackles"... everyone laughed.

Warnock views Pep Guardiola as the best manager of his lifetime, while the Spaniard praised the veteran's humour after once addressing his Man City squad at a training session

Warnock has led teams to promotions on eight occasions over the course of his career

'After the session we had a coffee and Pep said to me, "Neil, that was amazing, you know when you talked to the players? I understood why you had so many promotions".

'He started counting and said, "What we have is all these staff… computers, details, nutritionist, all these staff, but you know what we don't have? Humour". He noticed why my lads had done well in my teams, just in that meeting. It was good, that. He is amazing.

'Pep is the best manager of my lifetime. They say he had all the best players but it is not easy managing them. Pep did things with players and now there are non-league teams trying to play like Manchester City!'

Warnock is now doing stage tours - Guardiola attended one last season - and had a tear in his eye when he stepped out at London Palladium given he used to watch shows there with his mother, who was in a wheelchair, on the TV as a child.

So what is Warnock up to these days? His current role is advisor at Torquay United but last management job was at Aberdeen two years ago… so is he out of the rat race for good this time?

'No, not really, no,' he says. 'I only work from February to April! So the phone will be on after Christmas. You never know, do ya? There will be someone thinking "why don't we get that Warnock in?".

'I've retired 40 times! Every time I have said it, I have meant it. But it's that dressing room camaraderie. There's something about football, when I look at some of the managers now… they just don't excite me.

'I remember Ruben Amorim (breaks down laughing). He's got his computer out on the bench! I remember watching and thinking, "I'm sorry, son, you need more than a computer to help you tonight!".

Warnock is currently doing stage tours, with Guardiola among the attendees last season

Warnock's current role is advisor at Torquay United and briefly served as interim manager last season, with the 77-year-old admitting he had not completely ruled out a return to the dugout

'And likewise, I see them making notes on the bench, oh my god. I think "what are you doing, your shopping list for Tescos?".

'I do enjoy walking and I enjoy photography, believe it or not. I go up the river with my phone, there's so many lovely things to see.

'I've got an electric bike and I sometimes do about 25 miles. I was thinking of doing a cycle of all my clubs but that would take me five years! They go at about 30mph down the hills, you've got to be careful, you wouldn't want to come off them.'

He is also enjoying fishing, being with the family and playing golf with his son, a PGA rising star William - though Warnock Sr insists he often embarrasses himself playing off 'the ladies' tee'.

The thing that makes Warnock most proud is the four promotions at Wembley but also the togetherness he fostered in his many teams.

He tells us: 'What I like about the teams I had, they all have reunions. You look at the tele now, someone will score a goal and kiss the badge… they won't have a reunion.

'When I go to these reunions, I see all my lads and how I blended that dressing room together and I look at the comradeship they still have now, they are the same as they were just a lot older.

'This year, my Scarborough team are having a 40-year celebration and the lads have invited me. I said there's no way I'm going out with that lot after the do because they can drink, let me tell you!'

She also criticised the tribute to her son. Portugal's players walked onto the pitch wearing his number seven shirt, while fans applauded in the seventh minute, but Dolores Aveiro claimed:

“The tribute should have been paid in his presence. It’s here, at Sporting, that we’re going to pay tribute to him. Here, they recognise his worth.”

Finally, she said: “With the national team, he was not respected, not even by his teammates.”

Portugal have come up with a genius way to 'retire' Cristiano Ronaldo's number seven shirt.

It'll come as no surprise that the post-defeat focus has been on Ronaldo. When asked about the player directly after the Denmark game, Jesus was asked if he missed the player. He replied: “Missing what? He’s no longer on the national team, so what’s missing? The only thing missing is his presence here to keep me company.”

Now, ahead of their game against Wales on Tuesday night, the Portugal boss was asked what he thought about Ronaldo's mother's comments. He fired back:

“Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother?”

He added: "Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother is a lady I respect greatly. A mother is still a mother, there’s nothing you can do about it. I understand her statements.”

Despite the constant focus on the retired star, Jesus said he was happy to keep discussing the matter long into the future, concluding: “I don’t know when it’s going to stop. If you guys (reporters) ask the questions, I have to answer. If you ask about Ronaldo next year, I will answer.”

#1276. Report Fabregas was targeted by Manchester United before Pochettino decision

Como coach Cesc Fabregas was discussed by Manchester United before they reached an agreement with Mauricio Pochettino, claim The Athletic, after crushing the team 4-1 in the Champions League.

The Premier League side began making genuine plans to sack Michael Carrick after that humiliating result at the Stadio Sinigaglia last month, although they waited until the break for international duty to pull the plug.

They have paid circa £9m to buy Pochettino and his staff out of their contracts with the USMNT, announcing their new coach.

According to The Athletic, Pochettino was by no means top of the wish list when Manchester United directors began parsing the options to replace Carrick.

It is no secret that Unai Emery of Aston Villa was one of their first targets, but the 55-year-old was not interested in leaving the current project when signed on until 2029.

Another potential candidate was current Brighton and Hove Albion boss Fabian Hurzeler, but the price quoted to them for breaking that contract would’ve been £15m.

It is reported that Fabregas was discussed, but that it never even got so far as a formal approach to the Spaniard or Como.

This would’ve been ill-fated, because Inter had already tried to poach Fabregas last summer and were rejected outright by the club’s rich Indonesian owner Mirwan Suwarso.

The idea of letting the coach leave mid-season would’ve been even more improbable, especially just weeks after beating this Manchester United team in the Champions League, then crushing RC Lens 9-1.

Enzo Maresca’s flawless start to the Premier League with Manchester City is over after another masterclass from Unai Emery.

Matches at Villa Park were a notoriously chastening experience for Pep Guardiola and it was the same old story for Maresca as City have now lost on their last four visits here.

On his fourth anniversary in charge of Villa, there was more tactical brilliance from Emery, who also did the double over Guardiola last season. It was Emery’s £65m record signing Nicolas Jackson who again underlined how some managers can get the best out of certain players.

City’s run of seven league wins in a row always looked in danger here against a vibrant and energetic Villa. Maresca will also reflect on two poor goals conceded after errors from Marc Guéhi and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.

Guéhi endured a particularly difficult afternoon and was at fault for Jackson’s stunning first goal. The centre-back has struggled in recent weeks with a bad mistake in England’s defeat by Spain and he was exposed for both Ipswich goals last week. He was replaced at half-time after a booking for a foul on the excellent Jackson.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Aston Villa vs Manchester City.

Premier League leaders City will attempt to maintain their flawless start to the season when they visit Villa Park for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off.

The match marks the first meeting between the sides since the final weekend of last season, when Villa secured a 2-1 victory at the Etihad in Pep Guardiola’s final game in charge at City.

Enzo Maresca became the first manager in City’s Premier League history to win his opening seven fixtures, lifting his side three points clear of title holders Arsenal. Only Chelsea in 2005-06 and Liverpool in 2019-20 have managed a longer winning start to a top-flight campaign. Following a 3-2 victory against Ipswich Town last weekend, City rebounded from a European setback against Paris Saint-Germain by delivering a commanding 5-1 Champions League win over AEK Athens on Wednesday.

However, Unai Emery’s side will present a formidable challenge. Aston Villa enter the contest on a seven-match unbeaten streak across all competitions, headlined by a perfect record in the Champions League following midweek success against Viking FK.

Villa’s domestic form has also improved, taking seven points from their last three league outings, including a 1-0 away victory at Newcastle United in Emery’s 100th Premier League match as manager. Sitting 12th in the table, Villa remain on the hunt for their first home league win of the season, though their impressive European performances at Villa Park provide significant momentum.

Emery’s men completed a league double over City last term, including a 1-0 win on home turf. Should Villa claim victory again on Saturday, it would mark the first time in the Premier League era that they have recorded three consecutive victories over the Manchester club.

#1274. Steven Gerrard Has Theory About Why Man Utd Hired Mauricio Pochettino

Former Liverpool and England midfielder Steven Gerrard has offered an eye-opening theory as to why Manchester United opted for Mauricio Pochettino over Eddie Howe in their search for a replacement for Michael Carrick.

The Red Devils announced their agreement with the then-USMNT head coach on Friday, officially ushering in a new era at Old Trafford after the previous one burned out almost as quickly as it began. United had managed just three wins from their opening 15 games of the 2026/27 season, including just one in the Premier League, leaving them languishing in the relegation zone by November.

While it initially appeared that United's hierarchy were leaning towards Howe as their next manager, they ultimately moved quickly to get the paperwork over the line for former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino.

His ability to build a strong dressing-room culture, develop young players and oversee steady progress makes him more of a long-term project manager than someone whose candle burns at both ends. However, Gerrard believes there was another, perhaps even more significant, reason why Pochettino ultimately got the nod.

On a recent episode of The Overlap, Gerrard was asked why United opted for Pochettino as opposed to other available candidates. He claimed: "I think he would have been on their list for a long time, so they've admired him for a long time. They probably haven't been able to get him for different reasons, timing.

He's a good man manager. Players like to work for him. You listen to all the interviews when he left Spurs, Harry Kane, Dele Alli, Kyle Walker, they all loved having him as their manager. And if he can hit the ground running at Manchester United, you can see it being a real positive appointment.

"But the other thing to mention, I think, which is interesting, is if you look at Manchester United's main players, I know some of them are coming to the end of their contracts, but Lisandro Martinez, Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha, your Amad Diallo's of this world, he will speak Spanish.

"So, if he can get these players back into top form and enjoying themselves and smiling again, that's a large chunk of this Manchester United team. "I think that will have had an impact as well, because if you look at Eddie Howe, he was available as well and it seemed as if they wanted the Pochettino road."

He continued: "You wonder whether the Spanish-speaking thing has had a bit of an impact, because you look at a lot of the main players in that Manchester United team and squad.

"The Spanish-speaking could go a long way, I would say. And him being able to speak different languages might have been the reason why he's just been picked over Eddie.

The Argentine's backroom staff have been given the green light to start work at Carrington early

"I don't know whether Eddie was a serious contender or not, but from afar, I think they would have been stupid not to have him on the list. I'm a massive fan of Eddie Howe as well, but you can understand maybe why they've gone down the Pochettino road."

A likeable, well-to-do manager who has a track record of helping teams improve over time - there's a lot to love about Pochettino, and there are a lot of things that show he could be the one to finally get United back on track in their disastrous post-Sir Alex Ferguson era.

Taking Tottenham from outside of the European qualification places in 2014 to the Champions League final five years later is good evidence of that. But it's also that timeframe that may suggest there's a missing piece to his record.

Besides a stint with PSG, who are always expected to win league titles at ease, the Argentine has never won a major honour in his managerial career.

That will absolutely have to change if he is to make a success in what has become known as 'football's most stressful job.' But, at the same time,ime will also have to be given more time than his predecessors for any chance of that, given he's a slow-burner rather than a quick burner like that of other candidates such as Antonio Conte.

His first test will come in a trip to Anfield to take on Liverpool next Sunday afternoon - a place he has had joy at in the past with Southampton, and a place he could make a dream start to lfie as United boss.

#1273. England's evolution: James Trafford and two other stars chisel their names into the XI, Thomas Tuchel learning from Argentina and Jude Bellingham playing like a captain!

Published: 02:32 EST, 16 November 2026 | Updated: 09:25 EST, 16 November 2026

England ended world champions Spain's 43-match unbeaten run in dramatic fashion with a 3-2 win on a memorable night in Madrid.

After Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White scored to establish a three-goal lead, the visitors had to cling on after Elliot Anderson was sent off and the hosts scored twice in the final half hour.

The victory means Thomas Tuchel's side top their Nations League group and it provided a strong riposte to criticism of the manager following the World Cup semi-final defeat by Argentina in July.

Our chief football reporter, Craig Hope, was at the Metropolitano Stadium, and here are his FIVE big take-aways…

It would not have mattered had England conceded a late equaliser. To draw comparison with Argentina in the final half hour is unfair and inaccurate. The World Cup semi-final was 11v11 and so, when we draw conclusions from this game, let us do so on the same terms.

Thomas Tuchel was delighted with his England players as they won 3-2 away in Spain

And what did England do at 11v11 with a 1-0 lead? They attacked. And attacked again. This was a major change (and improvement) and is the reason for such encouragement. They have learnt from a mistake, as much as Tuchel will be loathe to admit.

Mexico would be a fairer parallel, but that was against opposition far inferior to Spain. At 11v10, we could not expect England to stay on the front foot here, as they were until the point of Jarell Quansah's needless mistake and Elliot Anderson's subsequent red card.

And that is cause for great optimism - because this game was not in the balance in any way when the teams were at equal number.

For me, and I don't think this is even close, this was the best performance of Tuchel's reign.

Do England suddenly have a pair of full backs?! After years of trawling and trialling, here in the most testing of surrounds, Ben White and Lewis Hall inked their names into Tuchel's XI.

We can forgive the concession of two goals when down to 10 men - because with 11, Spain barely looked like getting a shot on target. In fact, they didn't.

Much of that was down to the solidity of the full backs. Then, with backs to the wall, the pair became bricks in the resistance. One White block late on was heroic.

Before that, Hall's best work was not in containing Lamine Yamal, but in emulating him. His dribbles were daring and unnerved Spain, who thought they would spend the game in England's half and with the ball. They did neither early on and Hall was central to that.

White's goal had shades of Carlos Alberto on the overlap, and his England redemption arc felt like it reached completion here. Let him now move on now, for England need him.

No more boos, please, only cheers for White (and Hall).

It's time to stop the boos for Ben White after he starred with Lewis Hall at full back

Ezri Konsa is England's best defender. Build the backline around him.

Tuchel said on the eve of the game that he thought Konsa had grown for the move to Arsenal, and this was proof.

Boy do England need a mature, reliable presence at the heart of their defence. Konsa showed here why he can be that man. He scored a fine goal, which is always a sign of a defender ready to take wider responsibility, but it was his cool interceptions and desperate blocks at the other end that were most reassuring.

What Konsa has to do now is build on this - and a man-of-the-match performance at the home of the world champions is a pretty lofty and solid foundation from which to do so.

Tuchel will, and should, be giving serious thought to keeping James Trafford in England's goal for the Nations League quarter-finals.

Jordan Pickford has done nothing wrong. And yet, it feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and here was his justification.

Trafford can be a little erratic and immature. What better way to grow, emotionally, than with a series of saves to preserve an historic win. He will feel like a different player, and person, to the one who started this game. Like White and Hall, this felt like a coming-of-age night in an England jersey.

Trafford has all the tools. He might just have used them to chisel his name into that team-sheet.

Goalkeeper feels like one position the manager wants to evolve - and James Trafford starred

Spain's fans are left shocked as Ezri Konsa hails the brilliant Trafford in emphatic fashion

No goals, but England would not have won this game without Bellingham. He terrified Spain, perhaps given their intimate knowledge of his brilliance.

Beating the best is as much a mental challenge as it is physical, and Bellingham believed. He made England believe, too.

His swagger. His majesty. And yes, his skill. Of all the positives from this win, it is hard to look past Bellingham as the biggest reason for England being able to challenge Spain at the top of the world rankings.

Jude Bellingham played like a captain, dropping into midfield when down to 10 men

He won the corner for the second goal and created the third. He then dropped into midfield when down to 10 and played like a captain.

That is what England need - Bellingham the leader, not Bellingham the individual. He has bought into the collective under Tuchel and, with that, his team-mates are buying into his big ideas. They don't come much bigger than what England achieved here.

#1272. Ex-Milan director on Cisse pursuit, Amorim ‘courage’ and 20-year-old talent

Former Milan director Geoffrey Moncada reveals how long they had been tracking Alphadjo Cisse, convincing him to choose them rather than PSV Eindhoven, and Ruben Amorim’s ‘courage.’

The versatile figure just turned 20 last month and received his senior Italy debut in last night’s 4-1 Nations League defeat to Belgium.

He earned that opportunity thanks to his club form at San Siro, scoring eight goals in 13 appearances between Serie A and the Europa League so far this season.

“We had a scout in Verona and he told us about this young lad playing in their Under-17 team, and he was completely different to the usual profile you get in Italian youth academies,” Moncada told Calcio e Pepe podcast.

“He could play as a support striker, a winger, a mezz’ala in midfield, a Number 10. He seemed to change position in practically every match. His ability to change direction was remarkable, he could also cross with his left or right foot, it’s so hard to find players who can do all that.”

Verona loaned Cisse to Catanzaro in Serie B and his performances there prompted interest from other clubs, above all PSV Eindhoven, who were very close to an agreement.

“We’d been working on Cisse for several years, so Verona knew that well, but timing can be the most important thing in transfers. We had to rush, otherwise PSV Eindhoven would’ve got him, and if he had then played in the Champions League, the price tag would go up to €30-40m,” explained Moncada.

“It wasn’t easy, because we couldn’t promise him regular playing time, but fortunately we have the name AC Milan and that has a certain effect, especially for an Italian player. So PSV could promise he’d be a regular starter, but it’s not Milan, it’s not the same for his family, for the player, or his agent.

“As soon as he heard our name, he made his decision. He knew what he wanted.”

Nonetheless, few expected Cisse to make such an immediate impact at Milan, and that was thanks to coach Amorim deciding to bet on him from pre-season.

“When he was at Manchester United, Amorim had done something interesting with Patrick Dorgu,” continued Moncada.

“Initially, the player was used as a left-back, but then was used on the right wing in the Premier League. Whether it works or not, this is a coach with courage, he is not afraid of making decisions or changing positions.

“Considering Milan missed out on the Champions League last season, getting a player who was at Catanzaro and throwing him into the starting XI at Milan, that takes courage.”

#1271. Saliba has fight on his hands to usurp ‘unbelievable’ Konsa

From the moment Ezri Konsa pulled on an Arsenal shirt, he has moved with all the composure of a man who knows exactly where to be and when. The centre-back has required no adaptation period in north London, where he has filled the considerable shoes of William Saliba with such class that Arsenal have hardly missed the Frenchman at all.

The loss of Saliba to a long-term back injury was supposed to be a major problem for Arsenal. Instead, the situation has now reached a point where some fans are wondering how Saliba will get back into the side. That may prove a little extreme, but the fact there is even a discussion is proof of Konsa’s superb impact at the Emirates Stadium.

“Unbelievable,” Mikel Arteta, the Arsenal manager, said of his £55m signing. “He’s come to a huge club and to position yourself in that manner, and to perform at the level he is, it is very difficult to do. We are really lucky to have him.”

In Arsenal’s latest victory, their seventh from eight matches in the Premier League this season, Konsa offered all of his usual defensive security and calmness in possession. Even more excitingly, he also scored his first goal for the club, smashed in from close range after a corner had caused chaos in Everton’s penalty area. It was Arsenal’s first set-piece goal of the season.

“I have been waiting to score my first goal for a while,” Konsa said. “I spoke to the set-piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well. We felt as players that it was coming, and today was the day.”

Some eyebrows were raised when Arsenal paid such a large fee to sign Konsa from Aston Villa. The Villa fans, though, were not among those who questioned the price or the player’s ability. They have known for years at Villa Park that Konsa is a player of the highest quality, and they will not be surprised by his exceptional start to his Arsenal career.

The same is true of the Arsenal players. Arteta asked the England internationals in his squad about Konsa before buying him, and the feedback was overwhelmingly positive. Konsa was already close friends with Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze before completing his transfer from Villa.

Konsa’s start to life at Arsenal is all the more impressive because he did not even have a pre-season. He effectively came straight from the World Cup into the club, and has been starting games since early September. His first start was against Chelsea, when he endeared himself to the home fans with a crunching tackle on former team-mate Morgan Rogers.

Konsa, 29, has quickly built a strong relationship with Gabriel Magalhães, his defensive partner who scored Arsenal’s other goal here against Everton, from Ben White’s cross. For both centre-backs to find the net felt like a throwback to last year, when Arsenal were so dangerous from crosses, and underlined how Arteta’s team are capable of hurting their opponents in many different ways.

The nature of the goals might give a misleading impression of Arsenal’s performance, though. This was not a gritty win. Arteta’s side produced some excellent passing moves and circulated the ball with menace throughout the game. They were also a little open at times, especially in the first half when Everton created a handful of decent chances.

Thierno Barry missed the best of those opportunities, with the score at 1-0. It was the closest the visitors came to hurting the champions, aside from some of James Tarkowski’s full-blooded tackles. “I felt we didn’t really get to a level that was good enough to get near them,” admitted David Moyes, the Everton manager.

The victory, combined with Manchester City’s defeat earlier in the day, put Arsenal level on points at the top of the table. Aside from the extraordinary thrashing at Brighton, Arteta’s side have looked just as solid, if not more so, than last season. That speaks volumes of the quality in the team, of course, but also says plenty about the way Konsa has adjusted to his new surroundings. Thanks to him, Saliba’s absence has not hurt at all.

“Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal – my first goal for the club – so a fantastic day overall.

“I’ve been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he’s been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today.

“I’ve come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It’s not surprising to me.

“We are champions and to be champions you’ve got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible.”

All over at the Emirates and the champions go level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table.

They kept another clean sheet and scored from a set-piece again. All is right in Arsenal’s world!

Oscar Bobb’s first Premier League goal for Fulham earned a 1-0 win over Coventry that lifted the Cottagers clear of the relegation zone.

Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to strike in the 80th minute as he twisted his way into the box and bent a shot into the far corner, only his second goal for the club in any competition since his £27million move from Manchester City back in January.

That was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, only a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign by edging out Hull 1-0 as the pressure continues to ease on Alvaro Arbeloa.

Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s side second-bottom of the table.

The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon which bought the CBS Arena back down to earth after their 4-1 win over Newcastle in their last home outing.

Odegaard drives a shot high over the ball as Arsenal close in on another clean sheet.

Probably sums up Zubimendi’s season so far that he finally gets some meaningful minutes in the Premier League and ends up getting smashed in the face and covered in his own blood. This is after he got injured in a cool-down a few weeks ago. When your luck’s out...

Brilliant play from Oscar Bobb as he cuts inside on his left foot and bends a shot into the far bottom corner for the away side.

Treatment is needed for Zubimendi after he is caught on the nose by Barry.

Big chance for Everton. Garner whips a teasing cross into the box, Dewsbury-Hall meets it with his head on the run but the ball flies just wide of the post.

Tarkowski is the latest yellow card for Everton after a foul on Havertz.

Eze with a poor cross into the box. He fails to run back quickly and Arteta sprints to the edge of the touchline and goes berserk at the midfielder.

How have Arsenal reacted to their top scorer Saka being injured? Both of their centre backs have scored for the first time this season.

On his 200 Premier League appearance for Arsenal, Gabriel marks it with his first goal of the season.

Garner is booked for Everton now after barging into Merino off the ball.

Arteta is shown a yellow card for something. Not sure what for yet. But the Arsenal manager is looking to make some changes off the bench.

Arsenal have been guilty of overplaying today. Opting for the extra pass rather than taking a shot. The game is open at the moment and that makes things dangerous for the home side.

Yellow card for Lewis-Skelly after bringing down Johnson. Gabriel is back on the pitch and seems happy enough to continue.

Arsenal have defensive options in Timber, Hincapie, Calafiori and Mosquera if Arteta wants to avoid taking any risks.

A worry for Arsenal as Gabriel jars his knee into the ground as he tries to clear the ball. The Brazilian is receiving treatment and hobbles off the pitch.

Arsenal get the match restarted. The longer the match goes on without extending the lead, Everton will think they have a chance.

Before today, Arsenal had averaged five corners per match in the Premier League this season. In the first 45 minutes here, they had 10 corners.

Yellow card for Mykolenko after he catches White wide on the right. Rice whips the ball in and Merino meets it with a flick goalwards but the ball goes over the bar.

That is the final touch of the half and the players are running off to get dry!
